turns.doctor_question: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?
turns.patient_response: Well, it's... I guess it started with the mail. Ever since those foreclosure notices started showing up, I just... I feel like I'm completely coming apart at the seams. I mean, I'm sitting in my truck crying before I even clock in. I jump every single time my phone rings. And at work—I'm a mechanic, I work on heavy equipment—I'm snapping at the apprentices over nothing, and I'm making these stupid, careless mistakes in the repair bay that I never, ever would have made before all this. It's just too much.

turns.doctor_question: Have you lost interest or pleasure in the things you usually enjoy doing?
turns.patient_response:
Yeah, I have. I just... I don't really have the drive for any of it anymore. I've completely stopped showing up for my church volunteering, and I dropped my fitness classes. I don't even go to the truck-club outings that I used to always keep up with. It's just too much effort to pretend I'm okay. 

And like I was saying about work... it's gotten bad enough there that my boss actually took me out of the high-risk repair bay. I just can't seem to focus or care about doing much of anything right now.

turns.doctor_question: Over these past few months, have you been feeling down or depressed for most of the day, nearly every day?
turns.patient_response:
I don't really think so. I mean, I wouldn't call it feeling depressed all day. It's more that I'm just completely overwhelmed and stressed out. 

Like I said, I'll cry in my truck because the pressure of losing the house is just so heavy, but the rest of the day I'm mostly just on edge and wound up tight. So, no, I don't think I'm walking around feeling sad or down all day long... I'm just stressed to the absolute limit.
